segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a man who had been lame from his mother’s womb was being carried in. Every day they would set him at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask for alms from those going into the temple.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to be given alms.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter looked intently at him, as did John, and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look at us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He fixed his attention on them, expecting to receive something from them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have, this I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And grasping him by the right hand, he raised him up. At once his feet and ankles were made strong,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and he went into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the people saw him walking and praising God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they recognized him as the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with awe and astonishment at what had happened to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he clung to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the colonnade called Solomon’s, awestruck.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Peter saw this, he addressed the people:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Israelites, why do you marvel at this, or why do you look so intently at us, as though by our own power or piety we had made him walk?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus, whom you handed over and disowned in the presence of Pilate, though he had decided to release him.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But you disowned the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be granted to you,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and you killed the author of life, whom God raised from the dead. Of this we are witnesses.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And on the basis of faith in his name, his name has made strong this man whom you see and know; the faith that comes through him has given him this complete health in front of all of you.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as your rulers did too.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But what God announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Messiah would suffer, he has fulfilled in this way.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Turn back, then, and return, so that your sins may be wiped out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: so that seasons of refreshment may come from the presence of the Lord, and that he may send the Messiah appointed for you, Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoration of all that God spoke of through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Moses said, ‘The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You shall listen to him in everything he says to you.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And it shall be that every person who does not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And all the prophets who have spoken, from Samuel and those after him, also announced these days.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, when he said to Abraham, ‘And in your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: It was to you first that God, having raised up his servant, sent him to bless you by turning each of you away from your wicked deeds.”

notes.note: Hours were counted from sunrise, so the ninth hour is about three in the afternoon. This was the time of the daily afternoon sacrifice in the temple, when people gathered to pray.

notes.phrase: the gate of the temple called Beautiful
notes.traditional: the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful
notes.note: No other ancient source uses this name for a temple gate, and its identification is uncertain. Many scholars connect it with the bronze Nicanor Gate on the east side of the inner courts. Luke uses the word for 'door' here and for 'gate' in verse 10, and both are rendered 'gate'.

Many manuscripts read 'rise up and walk'. The shorter reading translated here is found in some of the earliest witnesses. The longer one may have been influenced by similar commands in the Gospels, though the evidence is divided and some editions print the longer text.

notes.traditional: the porch that is called Solomon's
notes.note: This was a long roofed walkway lined with columns, running along the eastern side of the temple's outer court. It was a public space where people could gather and teachers could speak.

notes.traditional: his Son (KJV); his servant (most modern versions)
notes.note: The Greek word can mean either 'child' or 'servant'. Most scholars take it as 'servant' here, because 'glorified his servant' echoes the Greek version of Isaiah 52:13, the opening of the passage about the suffering servant. Older English versions rendered it 'Son'. The same word recurs in verse 26.

notes.traditional: the Author of life; the Prince of life (KJV)
notes.note: The Greek word covers both a leader who goes first and a founder or originator. It can therefore mean the one who is the source of life or the one who leads the way into life, and translators are divided. 'Author' is used in the sense of originator, not writer. Either way the paradox is deliberate: they killed the one from whom life comes.

notes.phrase: on the basis of faith in his name
notes.note: The Greek sentence is awkward and repetitive, and the translation keeps its structure. It does not say whose faith is meant, the lame man's or the apostles'. 'The faith that comes through him' could also be read as 'the faith that is through it', that is, through the name.

The Greek word is a title meaning the anointed king Israel expected, and here the title itself is the point: that this figure had to suffer. 'Messiah' is used where the word works as a title, and 'Christ' where it is attached to the name Jesus, as in verse 6. Several modern translations make the same distinction.

'Repent' now suggests mainly feeling sorry. The Greek word carries the prophets' call to change direction in mind and conduct and come back to God. Most translations keep 'repent' as an established term. It is paired here with a second verb of turning, rendered 'return', which reinforces the same idea.

notes.phrase: the restoration of all that God spoke of
notes.traditional: the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken
notes.note: The Greek can mean the restoration of all things, a restoration the prophets spoke about. It can also mean the establishment, that is the fulfilment, of everything God spoke through the prophets. The rendering leaves both possibilities open. The noun is related to the verb in the disciples' question about restoring the kingdom to Israel in Acts 1:6.

notes.phrase: The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me
notes.note: Peter quotes Deuteronomy 18:15–19, the promise of a prophet like Moses, and joins to it a warning worded like Leviticus 23:29. By the first century many read this promise as pointing to a single coming figure. The verb 'raise up' is the same one used for raising from the dead, and it returns in verse 26.

notes.phrase: by turning each of you away from your wicked deeds
notes.traditional: in turning away every one of you from his iniquities
notes.note: The Greek verb can be taken as transitive, with God's servant turning each person away from wickedness, as translated here. It can also be intransitive: 'as each of you turns away from your wicked deeds'. Most translations take it as transitive.

candidates.reason: As a title for Jesus (Acts 3:13, 26; 4:27, 30) and for David and Israel it can be 'servant', 'child' or 'son', and the choice should be uniform so the Isaiah echo is visible.
It occurs in Acts 3:15, 5:31 and Hebrews 2:10, 12:2, where translations vary between author, prince, leader, pioneer and founder, hiding that it is one Christological term.
With μετανοέω fixed as 'turn back', this frequent conversion verb needs a distinct, fixed rendering wherever the two are paired (also Acts 26:20).
It recurs in Matthew, Luke and Acts, and translators divide between the archaic 'alms' and 'charity', 'gifts to the poor' or 'acts of mercy'.
This epithet recurs across the Gospels and Acts alongside Ναζαρηνός, and a single decision is needed between 'of Nazareth', 'the Nazarene' and 'the Nazorean'.
